messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV-serving continuous-batching anomaly detected. Spike starting ~02:12 UTC. Symptoms: ~6x cache size increase on some shards, 15% tail latency regression, 3 customers seeing 503s. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/kv-cache
oncall-alex: ack. i'm on it, pulling logs and histograms now
oncall-alex: quick q — is this multi-region or limited? i'm seeing most errors from us-west-2
maya: seeing elevated evictions + paging to S3 on shard-43. KV paging rate x4. recent deploy shows batch-window change at 01:57
jonah: which flag name? `batch.window_ms` maybe? i can query flags
jonah: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/flags | jq '.["batch.window_ms"]'` shows rollout 40->200 at 01:57 (triggered by pipeline #2891)
deploy-bot: rollout: batch.window_ms=200 (canary 30% -> 100% started 01:58, pipeline #2891)
priya: that's it. increasing window lets more microbatching accumulate which ups KV write amplification and larger cache entries. if compaction/G1 doesn't keep up, eviction/paging cascade
sam-cs: affected customers: acme-inc (timeouts), beta-studios (latency spikes), plus one internal smoke job
oncall-alex: immediate mitigation options: revert rollout to previous canary, or apply per-tenant override for affected customers. i can revert canary if we agree
diego: prefer per-tenant override for acme first, and reduce global window to 60 ms as a precaution. then iterate.
maya: how fast can we set per-tenant override? admin UI is slower, CLI is fastest
jonah: CLI command ready:
```
# set per-tenant batch window override for tenant acme-inc
rwctl tenant override create --tenant acme-inc --flag batch.window_ms --value 40 --reason "live mitigation 02:20 UTC"
```
oncall-alex: executing now
incident-bot: Action logged: tenant override created for acme-inc by oncall-alex at 2479123460
oncall-alex: override applied. acme re-checking... 95th latency trending down
priya: i'll start staged rollback of the rollout percentage (30% -> 10% -> pause) and monitor cache metrics
deploy-bot: initiating partial rollback: set rollout -> 30% at 02:25 UTC. will monitor
maya: paging rate is trending down but some nodes still show elevated cache size and evictions
jonah: found an additional regression: KV compaction thread OOMs when batch write concurrency peaks. there's an internal kernel config that allows too many concurrent flushes — that amplifies disk pressure
diego: kernel change is higher risk. prefer flag-only mitigations first. if traffic still problematic, we can consider a hotfix patch after triage
oncall-alex: after partial rollback, global 95th latency back to baseline. evictions are still above baseline; lets watch for 10 more minutes
sam-cs: status update: acme & beta-studios notified via status page, account teams looped. acme requests override across all their shards (they're seeing hotspotting)
priya: ok we can extend the temporary override to 4h while we triage, but coordinate with account team for any long-term override
jonah: extending override command:
```
rwctl tenant override update --tenant acme-inc --flag batch.window_ms --value 40 --expires-in 4h
```
oncall-alex: update applied at 02:31 UTC
deploy-bot: rollout reduced to 10% at 02:34 UTC and paused
maya: no new 503s since tenant override. eviction rate down ~50% on impacted shards
incident-bot: Incident update: severity lowered to Sev2. Follow postmortem playbook: https://runbooks.internal/postmortems
diego: good work. next steps: assign postmortem owner, add rollout safety gates, and patch pipeline defaults to avoid rapid global rollouts
priya: i'll own the postmortem. immediate action items: 1) revert default rollout speed in CI/CD pipeline, 2) implement a rollout guard that pauses when projected cache growth > 100%, 3) add alert for batch-window changes that impact cache metrics
oncall-alex: handing off to priya for next shift at 03:00 UTC. timeline + logs saved to incident doc
priya: i'll also add a short-term dashboard and an automated check: if KV-cache-size increases > 2x in 5m, block rollout progress
maya: dashboards updated: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-cache-spike (charts: KV-cache-size, KV-eviction-rate, paging-rate, batch-window rollout %)
jonah: i'll open PR for rollout guard: pseudocode and tests included. PR link to follow.
sam-cs: i'll follow up with acme PM and share remediation timeline and temporary override details :white_check_mark:
oncall-alex: final note — create a staging test that replays large-tenant traffic with `batch.window_ms=200` to repro cache growth; add to nightly stress suite
jonah: agreed, adding test to `stress/kv/scenarios`
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for live operations. Please continue post-incident tasks in the PM doc.
